messages.subject: [Rd] [PATCH] PR#19144: wilcox.test / .psignrank upper tail precision and out-of-domain fix
messages.subject_clean: [PATCH] PR#19144: wilcox.test / .psignrank upper tail precision and out-of-domain fix
messages.body_plain:
Dear R-devel team,

I would like to provide an analysis, a minimal patch, and regression tests
for PR#19144 <https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19144>


The issue is that wilcox.test(exact = TRUE) can return a negative p-value
in an extreme-tail case.

Diagnosis
The issue arises in .psignrank() in src/library/stats/R/wilcox.test.R. When
zeros or ties are present, .psignrank() obtains a discrete probability mass
vector d from .dsignrank(). The probabilities are computed using
floating-point arithmetic, so their sum can differ slightly from one. For
example, in the n = 100 reproducer, I obtain:
    sum(d) = 1.0000000000000038
on x86_64.

For an observation near the upper end of the support, the current
implementation computes the lower-tail probability as:
    sum(d[s < e + 1e-08])
and obtains the upper tail by complementing this value:
    1 - y

In the reproducing case, the cumulative sum is slightly greater than one,
so the complement becomes:
    -3.774758283725532e-15
and the corresponding two-sided p-value is consequently negative as well.

More generally, when the cumulative probability is close to one, forming a
small tail probability by subtraction can also lead to substantial loss of
relative precision.

Proposed fix
Instead of obtaining the upper tail by complementing the lower-tail sum,
the proposed change sums the probability masses belonging directly to the
requested tail:

Index: src/library/stats/R/wilcox.test.R
===================================================================
--- src/library/stats/R/wilcox.test.R (revision 87400)
+++ src/library/stats/R/wilcox.test.R (working copy)
@@ -1101,13 +1101,12 @@
              seq.int(0, n * (n + 1)) / 2
     ## Density
     d <- .dsignrank(s, n, z)
-    y[i] <- vapply(q[i],
-                   function(e) {
-                       ## NOTE: C code in src/nmath uses a fuzz of 1e-7.
-                       sum(d[s < e + 1e-8])
-                   },
-                   0)
-    if(lower.tail) y else 1 - y
+    if(lower.tail) {
+        y[i] <- vapply(q[i], function(e) sum(d[s < e + 1e-8]), 0)
+    } else {
+        y[i] <- vapply(q[i], function(e) sum(d[s > e - 1e-8]), 0)
+    }
+    y
 }

 .qsignrank <-


===================================================================
This avoids the subtraction of two nearly equal floating-point quantities
when the upper tail is requested.

Verification
I tested the change using the reproducer from PR#19144 and additional cases
involving zeros and ties.

For the n = 100 reproducer, with rank sum q = 4755, an independently
computed integer generating-polynomial dynamic-programming calculation
gives the exact upper-tail probability:
    819334086710 / 2^99 = 1.292681258640963e-18.

With the proposed change, .psignrank() returns:
    1.292681258640968e-18
for this tail, corresponding to a relative error of approximately 3.9e-15.

The patch also removes the negative result in the original reproducing case
without requiring clipping or other post-hoc correction of the probability.

The accompanying regression tests cover:
- the original PR#19144 reproducer;
- p-value domain checks;
- comparison with the independently computed exact combinatorial reference;
- tail monotonicity; and
- additional cases involving zeros and ties.

I have attached the following files:
- wilcox_bug19144.patch ? minimal patch against the R sources;
- reg-tests-wilcox.R ? regression tests for the reported issue and the
numerical behavior described above.

I would appreciate any comments on the diagnosis, the proposed
implementation, or the form and placement of the regression tests.

Best regards,

--
Ahmed Sattar Jabbar
Department of Statistics | Mustansiriyah University
Baghdad, Iraq

Email:  ahmed.state.me at gmail.com
ORCID:  https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4614-735X

messages.subject: [Rd]  [PATCH] Include Linux distribution identifiers in the default HTTP User-Agent
messages.subject_clean: [PATCH] Include Linux distribution identifiers in the default HTTP User-Agent
messages.body_plain:
Simon,

thanks for the reply, and no worries about the delay.

You are right that the current User-Agent is documented, and calling it a bug was wrong on my part. The libcurl point is also fair: my patch would have dropped `libcurl/<version>` from the header.

I have since looked at the custom binary types added in 4.6.0 (r89368-r89372 and r89499). I will add the `bin/linux/<build>/contrib/<x.y>` layout to cran.rpkgs.com, so an R build with `R_PLATFORM_PKGTYPE` set gets binaries with no further setup. It **does not cover** the case I care about most, though:

1. `R_PLATFORM_PKGTYPE` has to be set by whoever builds or ships R. On Linux that means distribution packagers, people building from source, rig, and most Docker and CI images. None of them set it today AFAIK. When it is unset, R 4.6 requests `src/contrib` just like 4.5.

2. It cannot become a default in R. If R derived `pkgType` from os-release, every Linux user with the default type `"both"` would also request `bin/linux/<build>/contrib/<x.y>` from CRAN, which has no such directories. With cloud.r-project.org and R 4.6.1, `install.packages("cli")` then prints this on every call:

```
Warning: unable to access index for repository https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/x86_64-ubuntu-noble/contrib/4.6:
Package which is only available in source form, and may need compilation of C/C++/Fortran: 'cli'
```

3. R cannot check Linux binary compatibility from the platform information alone. The `Built` check from r89499 compares only the CPU and linux vs. non-linux, so in R 4.6.1 the following returns `TRUE`, i.e. a glibc binary passes on Alpine:

```r
utils:::.is.built.compatible("R 4.6.1; x86_64-pc-linux-gnu; 2026-09-01 10:00:00 UTC; unix", platform = "x86_64-pc-linux-musl")
```

I am not asking for a stricter check. It just means the repository has to pick the right binary, and for that it needs to know the system it is running on.

In R 4.6.1, `--vanilla` and the default libcurl method, a request for `PACKAGES` carries only

```
User-Agent: libcurl/8.22.0
```

so the server sees neither the R version nor the platform. Every Linux binary repository I know of works around this with a per-distribution URL, an `HTTPUserAgent` line in `Rprofile.site`, or both; Posit Package Manager [documents such a snippet](https://docs.posit.co/rspm/admin/serving-binaries.html#binary-user-agents), and rocker adds it in [`setup_R.sh`](https://github.com/rocker-org/rocker-versioned2/blob/2b8857e9bf3f87bb248d3d803bd3f32ff4d31ab0/scripts/setup_R.sh#L36-L40). Posit's own R builds have gone further [since 2019](https://github.com/rstudio/r-builds/commit/a54183792753d4df38db27dabdfb4455f78a7f3d): rstudio/r-builds appends the os-release `ID` and `VERSION_ID` to `HTTPUserAgent` in the system Rprofile, so even `R --vanilla` sends `R/4.6.1 (ubuntu-24.04) R (...)`The information is already being sent, but only from builds whose maintainers patched it in, each in its own format. **That is what I would like to fix in R itself**: the same repos setting, e.g. in an `renv.lock` or a CI matrix, should work on any Linux system without client-side configuration.

A revised proposal that leaves everything existing untouched:

- The User-Agent stays exactly as it is, including the `R (` rule in `libcurl.c`.
- On Linux, the libcurl method sends **one additional header**, built from `R.version`, the `ID` and `VERSION_ID` fields of os-release, and `gnu_get_libc_version()` (just `musl` on musl, which has no version API). Values are restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, as in the earlier patch. The header name is open to suggestions.
- An option, plus an environment variable for site-wide setups, turns it off (not sure if this is ever needed).

For example:

```
R-Client: 4.6.1; x86_64-pc-linux-gnu; distro=ubuntu; version=24.04; libc=glibc-2.39
```

On privacy, I think browsers are the wrong comparison here - package managers match better. `pip` sends the distribution and libc in its User-Agent:

```
pip/26.2.1 {"cpu":"x86_64","distro":{"name":"AlmaLinux","version":"10.2","libc":{"lib":"glibc","version":"2.39"}},...}
```

and conda sends `Linux/<kernel> <distro>/<version> glibc/<version>`. PyPI uses this for its download statistics, while wheel selection happens on the client through platform tags. R has no such tags for Linux binaries, so the header would serve both purposes: statistics for CRAN and mirror operators, and correct binary selection for repositories that offer Linux binaries.

If R Core is open to this in principle, I will rework the patch along these lines.

Best,
Patrick

P.S. While reading the 4.6.0 changes I noticed that r89370 changed the `install.packages.check.source` condition in `src/library/utils/R/packages2.R` to `grepl("^[[:lower::]]+[.]binary", type)`, with an extra colon. In R 4.6.1 this returns `FALSE` for every type, including `"win.binary"` and `"mac.binary"`, so the source-version check that 4.5 did for Windows and macOS binaries is now skipped.

messages.subject: [Rd] Ncell GC trigger reaches SIZE_MAX after grow/shrink/regrow in AdjustHeapSize
messages.subject_clean: Ncell GC trigger reaches SIZE_MAX after grow/shrink/regrow in AdjustHeapSize
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I found a reproducible node-heap sizing bug in R 4.6.0 on arm64 macOS.
After allocating and releasing a list, shrinking the heap with gc(), and
allocating a smaller list, the Ncell GC trigger becomes approximately
1.844674e19, although fewer than one million Ncells are live.

I encountered this while importing a large 3D scene into R, where
suspiciously high swap usage and memory pressure/compression prompted an
investigation. The import creates many small R objects, so delayed
node-triggered collection could let unreachable objects accumulate and
increase memory pressure. The base-R example below reproduces
the threshold failure without the scene or any contributed packages.

This reproduces in a fresh vanilla session using only base R. I also checked
the source at the installed build's reported SVN revision and stepped
through the failing calculation in the installed libR with LLDB.

Reproducible example
----------

Save the following as gc-trigger.R and run Rscript --vanilla gc-trigger.R:

    large = lapply(seq_len(2000000L), as.double)
    invisible(gc())
    rm(large)
    for (i in 1:16) {
      invisible(gc())
    }
    small = lapply(seq_len(600000L), as.double)
    print(gc())

Output:

              used (Mb)   gc trigger         (Mb) limit (Mb) max used  (Mb)
    Ncells  963857 51.5 1.844674e+19 9.851624e+14         NA  2783848 148.7
    Vcells 1863472 14.3 8.388608e+06 6.400000e+01      65536  5119567  39.1

Expected: an ordinary node-heap threshold appropriate to this small live
heap, rather than a threshold near the unsigned 64-bit maximum.

No contributed packages are needed. I reproduced this with R_GC_MEM_GROW,
R_NSIZE, R_VSIZE, R_MAX_VSIZE, R_MAX_NSIZE and R_GCTORTURE unset.

Please use a fresh process for this example. It also reproduces in a fresh
interactive R --vanilla terminal session, but may not reproduce in an
existing session. The predictor runs only during the first 49 node-heap
growth adjustments (adjust_count starts at 1 and the condition is < 50)
Its saved live-node count and the current heap thresholds also depend
on earlier allocations. Existing objects can therefore change whether this
particular sequence triggers the failure.

Source and runtime diagnosis
----------------------------

In src/main/memory.c at SVN r89956, AdjustHeapSize() keeps last_in_use from
the previous early-growth adjustment. The shrink path does not update it.
When another growth adjustment follows a sufficiently large decline in
live nodes, line 1200 evaluates:

    R_size_t next_in_use = R_NodesInUse + (R_NodesInUse - last_in_use);

R_size_t is size_t (src/include/Defn.h:1043). At the failing adjustment in
the installed binary, LLDB showed:

    R_NSize before adjustment:  1241534
    R_NodesInUse:                963857
    last_in_use:               2304622

The mathematical prediction is -376908. Unsigned arithmetic instead
produces 18446744073709174708. At line 1204, dividing that by R_NGrowFrac
(0.70) produces approximately 2.6352491533870252e19, which is outside the
range of size_t before the cast back to R_size_t.

The ARM64 instructions in this binary implement that conversion with
FCVTZU. Stepping over it produced 0xffffffffffffffff (SIZE_MAX). The
unlimited R_MaxNSize then permits the resulting threshold. Continuing
execution produces the gc() output above.

The unsigned wrap is defined arithmetic, but the subsequent out-of-range
floating-to-integer conversion is undefined in C. A standalone extraction
of the arithmetic with these observed values also triggers Clang's
-fsanitize=float-cast-overflow. Other architectures/compilers may therefore
show a different symptom.

Revision-specific sources:

    https://svn.r-project.org/R/!svn/rvr/89956/trunk/src/main/memory.c
    https://svn.r-project.org/R/!svn/rvr/89956/trunk/src/include/Defn.h

The complete AdjustHeapSize() function is also unchanged in the trunk
source snapshot I inspected at Git mirror commit
d75f6a2224865f9ac0bee065de99af817a3a65e6:

    https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/d75f6a2224865f9ac0bee065de99af817a3a65e6/src/main/memory.c#L1179-L1236

I have not built or run that trunk snapshot.

Workaround and tested fix
------------------------

In a separate fresh session, setting mem.maxNSize(5e6) before the reproducer
prevents the enormous trigger; my run ends with an Ncell trigger of
1,244,355. A finite maximum of 1e9 also worked in earlier tests. This avoids
accepting the erroneous growth request but it doesn't repair the arithmetic.

I built matched unpatched and patched copies of R 4.6.0 from the release
tarball. Its memory.c matches SVN r89956. Both builds use Apple clang 16
and GNU Fortran 14.2 on arm64 macOS, with identical configure options
apart from their isolated paths. The patch makes three changes:

  1. Treat decreasing live-node usage as zero predicted incremental growth.
  2. Compute the extrapolated threshold in double and require it to be
     strictly below (double) R_SIZE_T_MAX before converting to R_size_t.
  3. Check change <= R_MaxNSize - R_NSize, with R_NSize <= R_MaxNSize,
     rather than adding change before checking the limit.

In fresh vanilla processes, without a finite node limit:

                        Live Ncells       Ncell GC trigger
    Unpatched R              965367           1.844674e19
    Patched R                965315              1531118

The patched build also passes five repeated grow/shrink/regrow cycles
(triggers approximately 1.47-1.78 million), steady growth through eight
retained blocks, and five cycles with a finite five-million-node limit.
The unpatched build fails the unbounded cycle test on its first round.
An extraction of the patched function passes sanitizer tests for the
observed history, finite limits, steady growth, out-of-range prediction
and addition overflow.

R's core basic/development checks passed in both builds.

Based on these results, I recommend the guarded predictor and limit check,
plus a fresh-process regression test: running the reproducer late in an
existing test session may miss the early-growth window. My tests only
confirmed the reproduciber is fixed on this platform.

Environment
-----------

    R version 4.6.0 (2026-04-24), SVN revision 89956
    Platform: aarch64-apple-darwin23
    macOS Sequoia 15.7.3
    Attached packages: stats, graphics, grDevices, utils, datasets,
                       methods, base

Tyler Morgan-Wall

messages.subject_clean: Feature request: allow denominator n in var() and sd()
messages.body_plain:
Dear R-devel,
Would R Core consider adding an optional argument to var() and sd() to allow calculation with denominator n?
My motivation comes from teaching statistics through empirical distributions. For the empirical distribution assigning probability 1/n to each observation, the variance is exactly

mean((x - mean(x))^2)

The current var() applies Bessel?s correction. That is useful for unbiased estimation under i.i.d. sampling, but the uncorrected empirical moment is also useful for descriptive statistics and for teaching estimation by substituting the empirical distribution for an unknown distribution. These uses arise even when the observations constitute a sample.
One possible argument would be correction = 1, retaining current behavior by default, with correction = 0 selecting denominator n. The same argument in sd() would preserve its relationship with var().
There is already a precedent in cov.wt(..., method = "ML"). Making the choice available directly in var() and sd() would improve discoverability and avoid requiring a separate function for this basic calculation. Consistent support in cov() would also be desirable.
I found a related R-devel discussion from February 2019: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2019-February/077300.html
The argument name and scope could follow R Core?s preferences.
Thank you for considering this request,

Jordan Adamson
Assistant Professor, Economics Department
Thompson Rivers University

messages.body_plain:
A belated update to an earlier thread, and good news: R builds reproducibly!!

Special thanks for Kurt for assistance with an autoconf/m4 aspect (we longer
show a hostname which may differ if different nodes get assigned the
different builds that are compared), and to the powerhouse team of Kevin and
his assistance Claude :) (for staring down some gnarly aspects of how
internal packages 'tools' and 'methods' are built when R is built). Along
with an earlier fix I managed by myself ;-) and all the earlier patches we
had done already in 2017 (!!) we are now at a point where R builds
reproducibly.

We had already used an earlier variable PKG_BUILT_STAMP just for the Debian
side, now along with the 'more official' one SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. I will ensure
all my patches use only SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH -- which is cross-distro and will
ensure other builds besides Debian will be reproducible -- and ensure those
patches land in base R.

To recap as there had been confusion, and possible hesitation by e.g. Simon
who seemed to read all this as a way of interfering with how his overload of
build stamps in generated DESCRIPTION files is used where we lack
representation of built-version numbers in binary artifact filenames: it has
nothing to do with any of that. By default, Sys.time() is used as before in
all builds. But if and when a special timestamp env var is used (and will
standardize on SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH) then binary artifacts (when patched) use
this 'source archive time' when set instead of wallclock at the time of
building. When set, this makes two subsequent or almost concurrent builds
binary identical (as we also stopped representing build-machine hostnames and
other sources of differences).

All this is current in patches inside the debian/patches/ directory indexed
by debian/patches/series (and hence ignoring some other older ones there) at
the repo at https://salsa.debian.org/edd/r-base and more public browseable
mirrors such as https://sources.debian.org/src/r-base/4.6.1-9 for the current
(Debian) patch version.

Cheers, Dirk

Tyler <tylermw at gmail.com> ?????:

> I found a reproducible node-heap sizing bug in R 4.6.0 on arm64 macOS.
> After allocating and releasing a list, shrinking the heap with gc(),
> and allocating a smaller list, the Ncell GC trigger becomes
> approximately 1.844674e19, although fewer than one million Ncells are
> live.

Thank you for the report! I can also reproduce the R_NSize overflow on
Linux/amd64 when R is compiled using Clang, but not GCC. As you
mention, R builds with -fsanitize=undefined using both GCC and Clang
show a runtime error when the double -> size_t conversion overflows,
even if R_NSize stays fine.

R_size_t next_in_use = R_NodesInUse + (R_NodesInUse - last_in_use);
(gdb) p R_NodesInUse                   
$6 = 992417                            
(gdb) p last_in_use                    
$7 = 2332966                           
(gdb) p /x (R_NodesInUse - last_in_use)
$8 = 0xffffffffffeb8b7b                

R_size_t next_nsize = (R_size_t) (next_in_use / R_NGrowFrac);
// ../../../src/main/memory.c:1204:52: runtime error: 2.63525e+19 is
// outside the range of representable values of type 'long unsigned int'

GCC compiles this as:
                                R_NGrowFrac -> xmm5
                        (double)PTRDIFF_MAX -> xmm1
; convert next_in_use to double accounting for the sign flag set
mov      %rdx,%rdi     
and      $0x1,%edx     
pxor     %xmm0,%xmm0
shr      %rdi          
or       %rdx,%rdi     
cvtsi2sd %rdi,%xmm0  
addsd    %xmm0,%xmm0          ; (double)next_in_use -> xmm0
divsd    %xmm5,%xmm0          ; xmm0 / xmm5 -> xmm0
(gdb) p $xmm0.v2_double[0]
$35 = 2.6352491533870297e+19
comisd   %xmm1,%xmm0          ; result exceeds PTRDIFF_MAX? (yes)
...
subsd    %xmm1,%xmm0          ; xmm0 - xmm1 -> xmm0
cvttsd2si %xmm0,%rdi          ; failed conversion stores (1<<63) in rdi
btc      $0x3f,%rdi           ; flips bit 63 in rdi, leaving 0
                              ; rdi -> next_nsize
(gdb) p /x next_nsize
$51 = 0x0

Clang compiles the same code as:
                                R_NGrowFrac -> xmm3
                                next_in_use -> r9
movq      %r9,%xmm1           ; (double)r9 -> xmm1
punpckldq 0x101164(%rip),%xmm1
subpd     0x10116c(%rip),%xmm1
movapd    %xmm1,%xmm2         ; xmm1 -> xmm2
unpckhpd  %xmm1,%xmm2
addsd     %xmm1,%xmm2
divsd     %xmm3,%xmm2         ; xmm2 / xmm3 -> xmm2
(gdb) p $xmm2.v2_double[0]
$32 = 2.6352491533870293e+19 
cvttsd2si %xmm2,%rsi          ; failed conversion stores (1<<63) in rsi
mov       %rsi,%r9
sar       $0x3f,%r9           ; account for the sign bit?
subsd     0x1011f0(%rip),%xmm2
cvttsd2si %xmm2,%r10          ; stores PTRDIFF_MAX in r10
and       %r9,%r10
or        %rsi,%r10           ; r10 -> next_nsize
(gdb) p /x next_nsize   
$46 = 0x8000000000000000

Thus the branch

    if (next_nsize > R_NSize + change)
        change = next_nsize - R_NSize;

is taken on Clang but not on GCC.

I think that your patch is sufficient to avoid the next_in_use overflow
and the resulting invalid double -> size_t conversion.

messages.body_plain:
Dear R developers,

 

It's not a direct bug in R but a computational issue I report

because the error users see from `eigen()` gives no hint of its cause,

while this function is fundamental in numerous statistical and machine-learning

applications at the core of

R paradigm development.

 

Set-up: R 4.6.1 (Ubuntu 22.04 build), linked to the system OpenBLAS

0.3.20+ds-1 for both BLAS and LAPACK (`La_library()`:

`libopenblasp-r0.3.20.so`, `La_version()`: 3.10.0); Intel Xeon w9-3575X.

 

A well-conditioned 200 x 200 symmetric positive-definite matrix (eigenvalues

in [0.0143, 0.205]; `chol()` succeeds) makes

 

```r

eigen(A, symmetric = TRUE)

#> Error in eigen(A, symmetric = TRUE) :

#> error code 2 from LAPACK routine 'dsyevr'

```

 

| LAPACK | BLAS | `eigen(A, symmetric = TRUE)` |

|---|---|---|

| OpenBLAS 0.3.20 | OpenBLAS (default or SkylakeX kernel) | error code 2 |

| OpenBLAS 0.3.20 | OpenBLAS (Haswell kernel) | ok |

| reference 3.10.0 | OpenBLAS (SkylakeX kernel) | error code 2 |

| reference 3.10.0 | reference 3.10.0 | ok |

 

The reference libraries were loaded with `LD_PRELOAD`; the kernel was set

with `OPENBLAS_CORETYPE`. In a simulation study, 6 of 1,004 such calls

failed, and `MASS::mvrnorm()` stopped with them. The OpenBLAS side is

reported to Ubuntu (Launchpad #2040027).

 

R Installation and Administration, A.3.3 "Caveats", already warns that an

external LAPACK may carry bugs. Two small changes might still help users who

meet this error:

 

1. For INFO > 0 from `dsyevr`, an error message that says the

eigendecomposition algorithm failed internally and names the LAPACK in

use (as `La_library()` reports it), so that users can check the library

before their matrix.

2. Possibly, a retry with `dsyevd` (divide and conquer) when `dsyevr`

returns INFO > 0, as some numerical libraries do, since the two

This is the relevant part of the NEWS file

Changes in R 4.6.2:

  Bug Fixes:

    ? In plain-text help (Rd2txt), paragraphs are again recognized even
      when started with a non-indented Rd comment, fixing a regression
      in R 4.4.0.

    ? rhyper(N, m, n, k) now switches to the ?large? scenario when m +
      n is larger than .Machine$integer.max, preventing integer
      overflow, thanks to Jonathan Blood's report on R-devel.

    ? Fix long standing (Fortran compiler optimization related) bug in
      nlminb with constraints, thanks to Kasper Kristensen's PR#19086
      report and patch.

    ? Fix for PR#19100: seq.int was not handling non-vector along.width
      arguments properly. Thanks to Mitchell O'Hara-Wild.

    ? Wrappers now duplicate even a wrapped object that might be shared
      before returning a read-only pointer. This prevents cached
      read-only pointers from becoming invalid. Reported by Ivan
      Krylov.

    ? dummy.coef() becomes more robust to non-syntactic variable names,
      fixing PR#18468.  Thanks to Bill Dunlap and ?R Dev Day?
      participants Vincent Arel-Bundock, Cynthia Huang, Tina Rozsos and
      Marina Marinelli.

    ? Now PROTECT() in SubassignTypeFix, fixing PR#19110 thanks to
      Kevin Ushey.

    ? writeChar() in a multibyte locale counts characters and bytes
      consistently and no longer overflows, thanks to Kevin Ushey's
      report and patch in PR#19112.

    ? dim(a) <- vec now checks for too large prod(vec), thanks to Kevin
      Ushey's report and patch in PR#19109.

    ? Tweaks (including to the parsers) for the C23 behaviour
      (preserving const) of strchr, strrchr and strstr.  (By Brian
      Ripley and Duncan Murdoch.)

    ? make check-devel now works without recommended packages.

    ? <matrix>[[i, j]] with negative i occasionally gives no error but
      accesses previous content; thanks to Kevin Ushey's report and
      very simple fix in PR#19116.

    ? Quartz device now correctly draws long paths (work-around for
      Quartz built-in stroker breaking long paths). Thanks to R Dev Day
      @ useR! 2026 contributors, notably Tomek Gieorgijewski, report in
      PR#18680.

    ? strptime(ch, "...%OS<n>...") now disregards contiguous digits in
      "<n>", for symmetry with strftime(), fulfilling Frederick Eaton's
      wish in PR#17209, thanks to a patch by Suharto Anggono.

    ? strptime() now also returns NA for out of range "%OS" and a
      correct error message in some wrong multibyte cases, fixing
      PR#19117 comment #1 and PR#19122 by Michael Chirico;
      additionally, some overflow to Inf times no longer result in NA.

    ? strptime("0", "%w") in a "C" locale now works in valid cases,
      returning NA for invalid week numbers ("%U" or "%W"), fixing
      PR#19124 thanks to Michael Chirico's report and notably Suharto
      Anggono's analysis, also correctly fixing PR#15195.

    ? ksmooth(x,y, x.points=NULL) now returns an empty (x,y) pair
      instead of crashing R, fixing PR#19153.

      Additionally, also by Adam Berke?, x <- rep(999,0); ksmooth(x, x,
      x.points = 1) no longer writes out of bounds, fixing PR#19171.
      Ditto for ksmooth(x, x, n.points = 0), PR#19219.

    ? besselI(1, 1e11) and besselK(..) now signal a warning and return
      NaN instead of typically segfaulting, fixing PR#19175 thanks to
      Ben Bolker.

      Further, besselK(1, -1e11) and similar warn about too large |nu|,
      returning NaN rather than segfaulting, fixing PR#19196 thanks to
      Adam Berke?.

    ? text.default(.., col = numeric(0)) and similar no longer segfault
      in "instrumented" versions of R, fixing PR#19178 thanks to Jiang
      Yuancheng's fusion-fuzz and Ivan Krylov.

    ? R CMD rtags (on Unix-alikes) no longer fails from a bad escape if
      sh is bash or busybox.

    ? capabilities("X11") no longer incorrectly returns TRUE on a
      Unix-alike where X11 is not actually available when built by a C
      compiler without C23 enum base types, thanks to Trevor Davis'
      report and patch in PR#19180.

    ? predict(smooth.spline(..), deriv = -99) and similar invalid deriv
      values now signal errors instead of segfaulting, thanks to Adam
      Berke?' report and proposal in PR#19190.

    ? format(x, width = 2^31 -1) for an non-ascii character x such as x
      = "\u00e9" now signals an error as the required width is too
      large, rather than segfaulting, thanks to Adam Berke?' report in
      PR#19188.

    ? influence.measures() inadvertently wasn't updated along with
      dffits(), dfbetas(), covratio(). PR#19167 by Amal Tawfik.

    ? If wilcox.test(..., exact=TRUE)'s p-value is close to the 0 or 1
      boundaries, the calculation no longer suffers severely from
      cancellation, thanks to Tasuku Kobayashi's reports and Ahmed
      Sattar Jabbar's suggestion in PR#19144.

    ? Long stringed error messages are now protected from premature
      garbage collection, fixing PR#19210, reported and analyzed by
      Yuancheng Jiang.

    ? strsplit(str, perl=TRUE, bytes=TRUE) no longer accesses invalid
      memory in case str is an invalid UTF-8 string, fixing PR#19212,
      thanks to Kevin Ushey.

    ? isoreg(numeric(0)) no longer returns unallocated component yc,
      fixing PR#19224 thanks to Kevin Ushey.

    ? KalmanLike(1:5, list(1,2)) and similar no longer segfault, fixing
      PR#19217 thanks to Kevin Ushey and Adam Berke?.

  Bug Fixes (Windows):

    ? path.expand("~") and similar now should work correctly on Windows
      when the user name is not in ASCII and neither %HOME% nor %USER%
      environment variables are set, fixing PR#18949 thanks to the
      report and patch from Ivan Krylov and Mauricio Vargas's R Dev Day
      work.

    ? file.copy(*, date=TRUE) no longer opens files for exclusive
      access when copying the file time.  Consequently, the time _is_
      copied now and concurrent attempts to open the source file should
      work reliably, thanks to Kevin Ushey's report and patch in
      PR#19187.

messages.body_plain:
On 29 October 2026 at 10:02, bastien_chassagnol--- via R-devel wrote:
| Set-up: R 4.6.1 (Ubuntu 22.04 build), linked to the system OpenBLAS

That's dated / a mismatch.  Why current R but older BLAS/LAPACK?  I recommend
Ubuntu 26.04 or 26.10 if you want to engage with upstream.

It's also ... sort-of well known. Just rotate through the available BLAS /
LAPACK combinations. On a Debian / Ubuntu system is so easy that many (many)
years ago I wrote a package doing just that to compare and time with GPUs,
see https://cran.r-project.org/package=gcbd -- could use some love and an
update to current packages.

There is also flexiblas, already in Fedora and last I checked 'being
packaged' for Debian.

| The reference libraries were loaded with `LD_PRELOAD`; the kernel was set

You don't need to do that. `gcbd` just uninstall / reinstalls. If you check
the manual page, you can see how the `update-alternatives` command (a Debian
/ Ubuntu special) allows you to switch.  The number of available BLAS /
LAPACK varies from year to year but there are way more than just reference
BLAS and OpenBLAS. On my (26.04) machine just now

  $ apt-cache search libblas | wc -l
  33
  $ 
  $ apt-cache search libblas | grep -- -dev | wc -l
  16
  $ 

It's big topic, and if you check source (of e.g. R itself) you will often
find comments about precision varying. "Practical" numerical analysis has
challenges that more theoretical approaches may gloss over.

Dirk
